title: MAS-Architect: Declarative Multi-Agent System Design via Separation of Concerns
claim: Existing representations are rigid or entangle structure with implementation; ours separates topology from implementation, making designs flexible and verifiable.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, red ✗ lists vs. green ✓ list in ours
description: Three side-by-side rounded panels compare ways to represent a multi-agent system. The left, gray panel is the graph-based paradigm. It shows a fixed graph of cartoon role agents (Manager, Wiki Searcher, Analyst and others) joined by arrows, a pre-defined role pool below, and red ✗ marks for fixed node library, no loops and no branching. The middle, pink panel is the imperative paradigm. It shows a Python code window with comments pointing to implicit topology, a small node diagram, red ✗ marks for implicit topology, poor readability and untyped state, and a chain-link graphic labeled Coupled Structure. The right, blue panel is the declarative paradigm (ours). Its top Topology Layer is a flow diagram with Router, Searcher, Analyst and Start/End nodes. A Separation of Concerns banner sits in the middle. The Implementation Layer below has four robot agent cards, code snippets and green ✓ marks. The eye lands first on the titles and the dashed blue panel.
caption: Comparison of MAS representation paradigms.
abstract: The Automated Design of Multi-Agent Systems (Auto-MAS) has emerged as a promising framework for addressing complex reasoning tasks. However, existing approaches often suffer from structural rigidity and entangle the design of system topology with the implementation of individual agents. To overcome these limitations, we propose MAS-Architect, a framework that automates MAS design through a novel code-based declarative MAS paradigm rooted in the \textit{Separation of Concerns} principle. By decoupling topology planning from node implementation via a unified interface, our approach enables the from-scratch generation of task-adaptive architectures. We further employ a \textit{Distill-then-Explore} training strategy to optimize these designs. Comprehensive experiments on five benchmarks show that MAS-Architect sets a new Pareto frontier in the efficiency–performance trade-off: it surpasses state-of-the-art methods while substantially lowering token usage. Notably, the framework achieves a strong average accuracy of 78.7\% across benchmarks with an inference cost of only 2,533 tokens per query. Qualitative analysis reveals the autonomous emergence of advanced collaboration patterns, validating the generative flexibility of the declarative paradigm. Code will be available at https://github.com/ZJUHJ/mas_architect.
